zh: 他不但会说汉语，而且会写汉字。
en: He can not only speak Chinese but also write characters.
explain: 不但 comes before the first part, 而且 before the second.

zh: 她不但很高，而且很漂亮。
en: She is not only tall but also pretty.
explain: 不但…而且… adds a second quality.

en: I am tired, but I do not want to rest.
explain: 可是 shows a contrast: tired, but still no rest.

zh: 只要有时间，我就去看你。
en: As long as I have time, I will come and see you.
explain: 只要 gives the condition, 就 gives the result.

prompt: Which sentence says: As long as you come, I am happy?
en: As long as you come, I am happy.
explain: 只要 goes with 就. 才 goes with 只有.

en: I will go only if you go.
explain: 只有 goes with 才, never 就.

en: He gets up early in order to study.
explain: 为了 + purpose goes at the start.

zh: 为了看电影，我们去了电影院。
en: In order to see a film, we went to the cinema.
explain: 为了 gives the reason for doing it.

prompt: Which sentence says: In order to see Mom, I went home?
en: In order to see Mom, I went home.
explain: 为了 comes first, before the purpose.

zh: 他为朋友买了一个手机。
en: He bought a phone for his friend.
explain: 为 + person comes before the verb.

en: Mom cooked many dishes for me.
explain: 为 + person says who it is done for.

prompt: Which sentence says: She bought a lot of fruit for us?
options: 她为我们买了很多水果。
她买了很多水果为我们。
zh: 她为我们买了很多水果。
en: She bought a lot of fruit for us.
explain: 为 + person goes before the verb.

zh: 我想看一本关于中国的书。
en: I want to read a book about China.
explain: 关于 + topic + 的 describes the noun.

zh: 这是一本关于音乐的书。
en: This is a book about music.
explain: 关于 + topic + 的 comes before the noun.

zh: 根据天气，我们明天不去了。
en: According to the weather, we are not going tomorrow.
explain: 根据 + source starts the sentence.

zh: 根据老师说的，明天不考试。
en: According to what the teacher said, there is no test tomorrow.
explain: 根据 introduces where the information comes from.

prompt: Which sentence says: According to the map, we go right?
en: According to the map, we go right.
explain: 根据 comes before what it is based on.

en: Drink water first, then eat.
explain: 再 comes before the second action.

zh: 她一边听音乐，一边做作业。
en: She does homework while listening to music.
explain: One 一边 before each action.

zh: 我们一边走路，一边说话。
en: We talk while walking.
explain: 一边…一边… joins two actions at the same time.

prompt: Which sentence says: He talks while drinking tea?
en: He talks while drinking tea.
explain: Each 一边 goes before its verb.

en: This room is both big and pretty.
explain: 又…又… joins two qualities.

en: This phone is both good and cheap.
explain: 又 goes before each quality.

en: She is both tall and pretty.
explain: 又…又… already describes the degree, so no 很.

en: The more he talks, the faster he goes.
explain: 越 goes before each verb or adjective.

en: The more I study, the more I like Chinese.
explain: 越…越… shows two things growing together.

prompt: Which sentence says: The more I study, the happier I am?
en: The more I study, the happier I am.
explain: Use 越 twice, not 越 and 很.

en: He did not eat until twelve.
explain: 才 shows it happened later than expected.

prompt: Which sentence says: He did not come until nine?
en: He did not come until nine.
explain: 才 means later than expected. 就 means earlier.

en: We were already there at six.
explain: 就 comes before the verb.

en: I have just bought a phone.
explain: 刚 comes right before the verb.

en: Where were you just now?
explain: 刚才 can start the sentence.

en: What did you say just now?
explain: 刚才 means a moment ago.

en: He has been at home all along.
explain: 一直 means all the time, without stopping.

en: I have always liked Chinese.
explain: 一直 comes before the verb or adjective.

en: She is always happy.
explain: 总是 means always.

prompt: Which sentence says: He is always at home?
en: He is always at home.
explain: 总是 goes before 在.

en: I usually get up at eight.
explain: 平时 means usually.

en: We often go to that restaurant.
explain: 常常 goes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: He often watches films?
en: He often watches films.
explain: 常常 goes before the verb.

en: My phone is the same as yours.
explain: A 跟 B 一样.

en: These two cups are the same size.
explain: 一样 + adjective says they are equal.

en: Today is even hotter than yesterday.
explain: 比 + 更 means even more.

en: He walks toward me.
explain: 向 + person goes before the verb.

en: Please walk forward.
explain: 向 + direction goes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: He smiled at me?
en: He smiled at me.
explain: 向 + person comes before the verb.

en: I watched TV for an hour.
explain: 了 goes right after the verb, before the length of time.

en: I have not eaten for two days.
explain: Length of time + 没 + verb + 了.

prompt: Which sentence says: I have not seen him for a year?
en: I have not seen him for a year.
explain: The time comes before 没.

en: He eats first, then goes to school.
explain: 然后 starts the second action.

zh: 我先去了商店，后来去了医院。
en: I went to the shop first, and later to the hospital.
explain: 后来 means later, after something in the past.

prompt: Which sentence says: In the end he came?
en: In the end he came.
explain: 最后 usually comes first.

en: I have been busy recently.
explain: 最近 means recently.

en: I did not go to school the day before yesterday.
explain: 前天 is the day before yesterday.

en: The day after tomorrow is Saturday.
explain: 后天 is the day after tomorrow.

prompt: Which sentence says: I have not been out recently?
en: I have not been out recently.
explain: The time word comes before 没.

en: You should go to bed earlier.
explain: 应该 means should.

en: I should go home.
explain: 该 also means should.

prompt: Which sentence says: You should listen to the teacher?
en: You should listen to the teacher.
explain: 应该 comes before the verb.

en: You do not need to come.
explain: 不用 means there is no need.

en: You had better bring an umbrella.
explain: 最好 gives advice.

en: You had better go to bed earlier.
explain: 最好 comes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: We had better go now?
en: We had better go now.
explain: Time comes before the verb.

en: He seems very tired.
explain: 好像 means it seems.

zh: 这个电影看起来很好看。
en: This film looks good.
explain: 看起来 means it looks like.

prompt: Which sentence says: Of course I know?
en: Of course I know.
explain: 当然 comes before the verb.

en: He has finally come.
explain: 终于 means in the end, after a wait.

en: I read almost every day.
explain: 几乎 means almost.

en: He suddenly stopped talking.
explain: 突然 means suddenly.

en: Nobody wants to go.
explain: Question word + 都 + 不.

en: I did not eat anything.
explain: 什么 + 都 + 没 means not anything.

en: Go wherever you want.
explain: The same question word appears twice, joined by 就.

en: Drink whatever you want.
explain: 想 + 什么 + 就 + 什么.

prompt: Which sentence says: Sit wherever you like?
en: Sit wherever you like.
explain: Use the same question word twice.

en: I do not know a single character.
explain: 一 + measure word + 也 + 不.

en: He is not tired at all.
explain: 一点儿 + 也 + 不.

en: I waited half an hour.
explain: 半个 means half.

prompt: Which sentence says: He studied for an hour and a half?
en: He studied for an hour and a half.
explain: 半 comes after 一个.

prompt: Which sentence says: There are about seven or eight books?
en: There are about seven or eight books.
explain: Put two numbers side by side, then the measure word.
